A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FSLoRA work. All 23 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable, and their text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original RoBERTa and LLaMA fine-tuning results, baseline comparisons, sketching ablations, compression experiments, and 50-device experiments.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark and ablation results, including additional heterogeneity experiments and LLaMA-7B evaluations in Appendices C and D.

M1.justification: The sketched objective, random-k matrices, local updates, sparse uploads, and server aggregation in Equations (2)-(5) and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. New aggregation remarks and sketch-transmission details explain the existing procedure. Combining sketching with top-k compression was already evaluated in v1.

E1.justification: V2 retains GLUE and the same eight commonsense tasks but adds fine-tuning on Wizard, Dolly-15k, and Alpaca followed by MMLU evaluation in Appendix D. This substantially extends the represented training and evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: The 50-device evaluation changes from comparison with no-sketch Federated LoRA in v1 Appendix C.3 to comparisons with HeteroLoRA, FlexLoRA, and FedStackLoRA under new heterogeneous settings in v2 Appendix C. The main benchmark comparator trio remains unchanged. FedBCGD receives a conceptual comparison, not an empirical evaluation.

E3.justification: The reported default LLaMA-3.2 training budget changes from 750 to 500 rounds, and its sketching-ablation upload budget changes from 400× to 200× the global module size. New protocols introduce normal/heavy-tail rank distributions, varied Dirichlet heterogeneity, 100 devices, and a 10-device LLaMA-7B evaluation on 1,444 MMLU samples. The newly disclosed default partitioning does not establish that existing splits changed.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds systematic tests of device-rank distributions, data heterogeneity, and scaling to 100 devices. V1's GLUE convergence analysis and 50-device sketching-versus-no-sketching plots are removed. Existing rank, sketching, and compression analyses remain but are revised; the main sketching-ratio sweep drops the 0.25 setting.

E5.justification: Both versions report the main benchmark tables over three independent runs with ± values. Neither introduces documented seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new appendix tables provide point estimates without establishing a new repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The main GLUE table is unchanged, but commonsense accuracies and GPU hours are revised: FSLoRA's average changes from 77.9 to 79.4 and HellaSwag from 83.1 to 82.2. These are replaced results under a revised training budget, not established same-setting gains. V2 also adds Tables C.1-C.3 and D.1, revises LLaMA ablation/compression curves, and removes the original GLUE convergence and 50-device ablation results.

T1.justification: Assumption 4.2 replaces separate bounded sketching and sampling variances with a joint, gradient-dependent variance bound. Theorem 4.4 changes its stepsize restrictions and error terms; Corollary 4.5 replaces the large-T big-O statement with an explicit bound containing T^(-2/3) and T^(-1) terms. Appendix F substantially revises the proof and adds a stepsize-selection lemma and corollary derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: resource-adaptive federated sketching of LoRA modules, convergence guarantees characterizing sketching ratios, and accuracy/resource advantages over baselines. Additional evidence and more explicit wording do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds an aggregation-choice rationale and explicitly acknowledges the absence of real-device deployment. It replaces the BoolQ sensitivity explanation with an ARC-Easy overfitting caveat and revises the FedAvg convergence interpretation. New heterogeneity discussion includes an overstatement: Appendix C.1 says all methods worsen under heavy-tail ranks, although FedStackLoRA's average rises from 72.81 to 73.43.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link and documents previously unspecified Dirichlet partitioning and its default parameter. It also supplies rank-distribution construction, LLaMA-7B target modules and client ranks, MMLU sample/access information, and float32 communication accounting with shared sketch indices. These substantially expand reproducibility information; repository contents were not accessed.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to selective aggregation, SCAFFOLD, decentralized-SGD theory, and FedBCGD. It expands the motivation for higher-rank LoRA and adds Appendix B distinguishing FSLoRA from block-coordinate methods. The principal positioning against heterogeneous federated LoRA remains intact.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is consolidated and rewritten, while the appendices are extensively reorganized: implementation and dataset descriptions move behind the proofs, and an appendix contents page is added. Section titles and explanatory prose are revised throughout, and the Impact Statement is removed.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main text from two columns to one, merges the two main benchmark tables into Table 5.1, and adds resource, conceptual-comparison, and experimental tables. Numerous plots are redrawn with changed axes, legends, and sizing; the original GLUE convergence plot and 50-device ablation figures are removed.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical coverage and reproducibility through Appendices C, D, and G. However, unlike v1's explicitly large-T corollary, the revised corollary has an unresolved justification gap: Appendix F.4 applies the stepsize-selection lemma with d=H without accounting for potentially tighter restrictions in Theorem 4.4. The empirical and documentation gains therefore coexist with uncertainty affecting a core theoretical contribution, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
